name: Seriation, event dates and battleship plots (kairos / tabula)
title: Dating the repo market by its mix, like pottery in a grave
what: Order months so every repo segment rises then falls once; the order becomes a clock you can read.
pick_line: Make the clock survive OFR's bucket split, with a time-series bootstrap for its intervals.
data: Public OFR repo volumes (9 venue × tenor segments) and Form PF tab 8.27; descriptive only
one: The repo mix runs like a clock; hedge-fund borrowing growth leads its speed by 3–6 months.

left.sub: mean dating error, 2023–26 months (“last training date”)

right.sub: trained on 2018–22 only, dates unseen months by their mix

findings.h: Ordering 101 months by mix alone recovers the calendar.
findings.t: Seriated order vs calendar: Spearman −0.96. Porčić test: 248 total modes vs 286 for the random 5th percentile; no random order out of 1,000 did as well.

chart.title: Porčić test: total modes across 9 segments (fewer = cleaner rise-then-fall)

findings.note: CA axis 1 holds 69.3% of the mix variation. Seriation coefficient 0.52 (0 none, 1 perfect).

findings.h: Hedge-fund borrowing growth leads how fast the mix drifts.
findings.t: Form PF total borrowing growth leads mix speed: r = 0.56 at 3 months, 0.54 at 6 (Holm p = 0.009, 18 tests). It holds in both sub-periods; prime-broker borrowing alone does not carry it.

findings.h: Honest miss: a data-definition change moves the clock a full year.
findings.t: OFR split its ≤30-day bucket on 2025-08-14. Summed back, the clock still jumps from −0.51 to +0.50 years. Segment order is only loosely stable between halves (Kendall τ 0.28).

chart.title: The 2025-08 jump in the clock, as reported (years)

findings.note: The bar before the split is drawn at zero; the value is negative (−0.51 years).
